design: Each layer may be off, direct treatment, or an anchored floating marker. Modes are independent. A layer can declare direct unavailable if exact glyph ownership or data is absent.

initial.scope: orthographic Hanyu Pinyin initial token, not necessarily phonemic onset

final.scope: orthographic Hanyu Pinyin spelling remainder, not IPA rime

tone.scope: listed citation tone, not tone-sandhi or contextual reading

direct.implemented: source-aligned vector stroke coloring where mapped, with a segmented cell underline as fallback
direct.needs: verified path-to-component assignments for unsupported characters; independent visual and linguistic auditing

marker.implemented: individually colored chips adjacent to glyph

layers.data: 513 v0.4 component IDs with path references

direct.implemented: two independent narrow color edges around glyph for first listed orthographic initial and final; not glyph-stroke editing

marker.implemented: colored pinyin segmented into initial and remainder, attached below glyph

layers.data: citation pinyin first listed reading; all alternatives in inspector

direct.implemented: colored top edge of glyph cell encoding citation tone

marker.implemented: small anchored tone symbol with distinct color

layers.data: tone extracted from first listed Pinyin reading; not contextual sandhi

ui.implementation: native HTML radio controls with CSS :has() treatments; minimal JavaScript persists enabled layer choices
ui.mode_selection_scope: site-local, across homepage and 10 character atlas pages; saved by channel in localStorage when available; defaults remain effective without storage
ui.accessibility: textual cues accompany visible markers; high-level colors are not the only distinctions; radio controls remain keyboard accessible

rendered_glyph_geometry: source-aligned SVG glyph outlines for mapped characters in component-direct mode; native font glyphs in other modes and when geometry is not available
stroke_order_policy: stroke paths retain source indices for geometry-to-component ownership alignment; no handwriting-order encoding or training requirement
